In ensemble learning, combining multiple models with diverse characteristics is a well-established approach to improve overall performance. The trainable MFCCs are designed to be computationally efficient, enabling seamless integration into existing speaker verification pipelines. Experimental results on the VoxCeleb1 dataset demonstrate that the trainable MFCCs achieve comparable performance to traditional MFCCs, with the added benefit of reducing computational complexity. Furthermore, the proposed model exhibits improved resilience to noisy conditions, as evidenced by its superior performance in the presence of artificially introduced noise. The trainable MFCCs also facilitate the development of a more robust speaker verification system, as they can be optimized for specific scenarios, such as low-quality audio. Overall, the proposed model offers a promising solution for enhancing speaker verification performance in resource-constrained environments. Additionally, SEDL exhibits robustness to variations in system parameters and can be efficiently implemented in hardware. A comprehensive analysis of SEDL's performance is provided, highlighting its potential as a reliable solution for decoding overlapping signals. This work paves the way for the development of advanced communication systems, such as massive MIMO and non-orthogonal multiple access, by offering a practical and efficient solution for decoding overlapping signals. identifying the most relevant parts of an image. Our proposed method employs
a non-convex energy function that is optimized using a primal-dual algorithm.

that encourages the model to focus on the image's most informative regions and
a regularization term that promotes smoothness. Our approach is unique in that
it does not rely on global image features, instead leveraging local information
to identify salient regions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our method can
be adapted to incorporate additional constraints, such as boundary conditions, to
further enhance its performance. Our experimental results, conducted on the
ADE20K dataset, show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art
techniques. The code and pre-trained models for our method are available on
GitHub at https://github.com/bertranddassorce/ncnc. Our work is the first to
utilize non-convex energies for salience identification, and we believe that
this approach has the potential to be applied to other computer vision tasks.

creation of memory-safe, multi-language applications that can execute securely.

can serve as a foundation for secure memory management in multi-language
applications.

Functional connectivity analysis in fMRI data is a crucial step in understanding brain function and identifying neurological disorders. However, the accuracy of these analyses can be compromised by the presence of noise and artifacts. To address this issue, we developed a novel approach that combines voxel-level and regional functional connectivity analysis to improve the estimation of inter-regional connections. Our method, which is based on a graph-theoretic framework, uses a weighted network to model the relationships between brain regions. By applying this approach to fMRI data, we were able to achieve higher accuracy in estimating inter-regional connections compared to traditional methods. Furthermore, the results suggest that our approach can provide more accurate estimates of inter-regional connections, which can be useful for understanding brain function and identifying neurological disorders. The assessment of coronary artery calcium (CAC) is a crucial tool for evaluating cardiovascular risk and monitoring disease progression. However, the process of quantifying CAC is often hindered by the need for extensive manual annotation, which can be time-consuming and prone to errors. To address this challenge, we propose a novel generative approach that enables the automatic segmentation of CAC from non-contrast CT scans. Our method utilizes a generative adversarial network to produce high-quality images of CAC, which can then be used to train a segmentation network. By leveraging this approach, we can generate a large dataset of annotated images, facilitating the development of more accurate CAC segmentation models. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in producing high-quality images of CAC, which can be used to train a robust segmentation network. Furthermore, the generated images can be used to augment existing datasets, enabling the creation of more diverse and representative training sets. Our results show that the generated images can be used to improve the performance of CAC segmentation models, even when used in conjunction with limited annotated data. This approach has the potential to revolutionize the field of CAC assessment by enabling the automatic segmentation of CAC from non-contrast CT scans. The widespread adoption of LiDAR technology in autonomous vehicles and robotics has led to a significant increase in the availability of point cloud data. However, the existing datasets are limited in size and scope, hindering the development of robust and reliable algorithms. To address this limitation, we introduce SynthCity, a large-scale synthetic point cloud dataset, comprising 1,000,000 points, generated using a combination of procedural city modeling and physics-based rendering techniques. Our dataset is designed to mimic real-world scenarios, with diverse environments, including urban and natural settings, and varying lighting conditions. We also provide a comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art point cloud segmentation algorithms on SynthCity, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses. Our results demonstrate that these algorithms struggle with segmenting complex scenes, underscoring the need for more advanced techniques. Furthermore, we showcase SSCAN's potential in real-world applications by successfully denoising hyperspectral images of the Indian city of Ahmedabad. The Government Documents dataset, Govdocs1, has been widely used in NLP research, particularly in the 2010s, to evaluate and compare various text classification and retrieval techniques. However, its limitations, including outdated content and outdated formatting, have hindered its contemporary relevance. To address this issue, we introduce NapierOne, a new dataset that replicates the structure and content of Govdocs1, but with a modern twist. NapierOne is comprised of 1,000 documents from 2019, sourced from the US Government Publishing Office, and is available in both HTML and plain text formats. Our analysis reveals that NapierOne exhibits similar characteristics to Govdocs1, including a high proportion of PDF files and a low frequency of HTML links. Moreover, we demonstrate that the dataset can be effectively utilized to evaluate the performance of NLP models, such as those based on BERT, in the context of text classification and retrieval. Our results show that the use of HTML documents can lead to improved performance compared to plain text, and that the incorporation of HTML links can further enhance retrieval effectiveness. Overall, we believe that NapierOne offers a valuable resource for researchers seeking to evaluate and compare NLP models in a modern, government-focused setting.
